messages:
maya_ml: FYI nightly eval alert for redwood-v2-small-quant — sudden jump in failure rate on the `customer-support` promptset :eyes:
maya_ml: eval-bot summary: 4.8% -> 18.2% failures overnight, mismatch in the first 20 tokens for many examples. link: https://dash.redwood/tests/2026/nightly/rv2-small-quant
eval-bot: [nightly-run] suite=customer-support, model=redwood-v2-small-quant, failures=182/1000, regressions=165, median-latency=42ms
jonathan: ugh. any signal that this is model quality vs infra?
maya_ml: quick diff shows outputs diverging at the prefix boundary in many cases. attaching a snippet.
maya_ml: ```
# golden: customer asked: "How do I reset my password?"
assistant: "You can reset by going to Settings > Security..."
# nightly: customer asked: "How do I reset my password?"
assistant: "Please provide your account ID so we can..."
# note: divergence starts after token 12 (end of system/prefix block)
```
priya: that looks like KV/prefix state leaking or being reused incorrectly. I ran a local reproducer with a fixed batch and saw the same nondeterministic branch when we enable prefix caching + small batch windows.
kevin_sre: yesterday we shipped a small change to batching window heuristics to improve throughput (PR 4893). It changes `batch_key` derivation for short sequences to collapse some keys for throughput. Could be related.
priya: that aligns — collapse/merge of batch keys may cause different prefix KV entries to share a cache slot when sequences are similar length. If two different prefixes map to same cache entry we can get stale KV used.
jonathan: can you reproduce with a deterministic sequence? steps?
priya: yes, simple repro: start two sessions with distinct prompts that share first tokens, enable prefix cache, force same batch id via short window. Observed outputs: one session returns tokens from the other about ~30% runs. Repro snippet:```bash
# repro harness (python)
for i in range(100):
  start_session(p1)
  start_session(p2)
  step() # flush batch
```
# observe mismatch at step 1 in ~30 runs
```
maya_ml: interesting — the eval diffs were concentrated on prompts that have similar system/prefix text (e.g., same policy header).
kevin_sre: temporary mitigation suggestion: revert the batch-key collapsing or mark prefix cache namespace to include full prefix hash. I can open a hotfix to revert.
jonathan: what's the perf hit if we disable collapsing?
kevin_sre: estimated 5-8% throughput drop for short sequences in our microbenchmarks, but correctness > perf for now.
priya: another short-term workaround: disable prefix-cache for the nightly eval runner or set it to mode=dedicated (no collapsing). We should also backfill tests that randomize session ids to catch this.
ops-bot: ticket created: INF-4821 — "Batch-key collapse causing prefix KV collisions -> nightly eval regressions" (assignee: kevin_sre) link: https://jira.redwood/INF-4821
jonathan: +1 on hotfix revert. Also add a unit test that asserts cache namespace is unique per prefix hash.
maya_ml: I'll gate the nightly runner to disable prefix cache until patch is in. Marking impacted promptset owners and pausing auto-alerts.
priya: I'll write the reproducible test and a small fuzz harness to try many prefix combos.
kevin_sre: I'll open the revert PR and the config flag to opt-out of collapse. Will post benchmarks here.
maya_ml: thanks — will follow up after revert lands. For tracking: if anyone sees similar spikes in other models, ping @maya_ml and post the eval link. :thumbsup:
jonathan: thanks team, good catch.
kevin_sre: PR-4930 opened (revert batching collapse), perf impact measured ~6% on short sequences, rollout plan: staged next deploy, rollback if perf unacceptable.
maya_ml: last note — adding this to the onboarding checklist: when enabling prefix caching for new quantized models, run the batch-key collision test.
priya: agreed. I'll add test to repo under `tests/cache_collision_test.py`.
maya_ml: closing loop here, will update INF-4821 with nightly re-run after hotfix. :white_check_mark:
